programs.nl_rule:
The input is a small rectangular grid (R rows × C columns) filled with colored cells. There are no special regions or background — every cell carries a meaningful color value.

Create an output grid of size (2R) × (2C) by tiling four transformed copies of the input in a 2×2 arrangement: (1) Top-left quadrant: rotate the input 180° (reverse both row order and column order). (2) Top-right quadrant: flip the input vertically (reverse the row order, keeping columns intact). (3) Bottom-left quadrant: flip the input horizontally (reverse the column order, keeping row order intact). (4) Bottom-right quadrant: place the original input unchanged. Equivalently, the output is the input reflected across both its bottom edge and its right edge to produce a point-symmetric 2×2 tiling.

The input grid has dimensions R × C (in the observed instances, 3 × 4). The output grid has dimensions 2R × 2C (6 × 8). The output is partitioned into exactly four quadrants, each the same size as the input. The center of the output is the point of 180° rotational symmetry.

content.text:
Let me start by showing the example via show_transformed_input (let environment compute gold) or show_example with my output. Let me verify the given example matches the rule.

Input:
```
7 6 7 7
6 6 2 2
2 2 2 7
```

rot180: reverse rows and cols:
rows reversed: [2,2,2,7],[6,6,2,2],[7,6,7,7]
cols reversed each: [7,2,2,2],[2,2,6,6],[7,7,6,7]

flipud: rows reversed:
[2,2,2,7],[6,6,2,2],[7,6,7,7]

fliplr: cols reversed:
[7,7,6,7],[2,2,6,6],[7,2,2,2]

original:
[7,6,7,7],[6,6,2,2],[2,2,2,7]

Top half hstack(rot180, flipud):
row0: [7,2,2,2 | 2,2,2,7]
row1: [2,2,6,6 | 6,6,2,2]
row2: [7,7,6,7 | 7,6,7,7]

Bottom half hstack(fliplr, input):
row0: [7,7,6,7 | 7,6,7,7]
row1: [2,2,6,6 | 6,6,2,2]
row2: [7,2,2,2 | 2,2,2,7]

Full output:
[7,2,2,2,2,2,2,7]
[2,2,6,6,6,6,2,2]
[7,7,6,7,7,6,7,7]
[7,7,6,7,7,6,7,7]
[2,2,6,6,6,6,2,2]
[7,2,2,2,2,2,2,7]

Yes matches. Good.

Let me demonstrate with a few examples. I'll use show_example with a new input so student sees it. Actually show_example requires I compute output myself and if correct it's shown. Alternatively show_transformed_input auto-fills gold — safer for correctness. But show_example lets me show pair too. Let me use show_transformed_input to guarantee correctness, showing a few varied inputs.

Then query_student on a fresh input, check correctness, then start_exam.

Let me pick varied inputs. Rule is general: R x C arbitrary. Let's use different sizes to convey generality.

Demo 1: 2x2 input:
```
1 2
3 4
```
Output:
rot180: [4,3],[2,1]
flipud: [3,4],[1,2]
fliplr: [2,1],[4,3]
original: [1,2],[3,4]

Top: [4,3 | 3,4], [2,1 | 1,2]
Bottom: [2,1 | 1,2], [4,3 | 3,4]
Full:
[4,3,3,4]
[2,1,1,2]
[2,1,1,2]
[4,3,3,4]

Let me use show_transformed_input with this.

Demo 2: 3x3 or 2x3 to vary. Let's do 2x3:
input:
```
1 2 3
4 5 6
```
Output 4x6.
rot180: [6,5,4],[3,2,1]
flipud: [4,5,6],[1,2,3]
fliplr: [3,2,1],[6,5,4]
original: [1,2,3],[4,5,6]

Top: [6,5,4,4,5,6],[3,2,1,1,2,3]
Bottom: [3,2,1,1,2,3],[6,5,4,4,5,6]

Full:
[6,5,4,4,5,6]
[3,2,1,1,2,3]
[3,2,1,1,2,3]
[6,5,4,4,5,6]

Good.

Let me send demos via show_transformed_input, then query.

I'll do multiple show_transformed_input calls in one block, then query separately (need to see result before exam).

Actually I can do shows and query in same block? The query depends on nothing from shows except student learning. But better sequential: show demos first, then query. Let me batch the two shows, then query.

Wait, guidance: "start_exam is held until your most recent query_student, made after your last demonstration on an input the student has not seen, came back correct". So I must query after last demo with unseen input and get correct.

Let me do shows first.

tools.name: show_example

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.
